match.reason: No bank point covers just shifts to a new equilibrium with both curves moving at once: eco-changes-equilibrium covers only single shifts, while e-equilibrium covers the both-shift case but is broader, also teaching equilibrium and market adjustment, and uses non-Victorian examples.

draft.title: Shifts and new equilibrium
card: Equilibrium is the price where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. A change in a non-price factor shifts a curve and moves the market to a new equilibrium.
a rise in demand (shift right) lifts both the equilibrium price and the quantity traded. A fall in demand (shift left) lowers both.
a rise in supply (shift right) lowers the equilibrium price and raises the quantity traded. A fall in supply (shift left) raises the price and lowers the quantity.
Both curves can shift at once. Then the effect on one of price or quantity is clear, but the other depends on which shift is larger.
draft.remember: Work out which curve moves and which way, then read off the new price and quantity.

a.q: A heatwave in Mildura raises demand for fans, and nothing else changes. What happens to the equilibrium price and quantity of fans?
opts: Price rises and quantity traded rises
Price rises and quantity traded falls
Price falls and quantity traded rises
Price falls and quantity traded falls
a.why: Higher demand shifts the demand curve right. This lifts both the equilibrium price and the quantity traded. A rise in price with a fall in quantity would fit a fall in supply, not a rise in demand.
a.clue: Demand shifts right along an unchanged supply curve.

b.q: In one year, a new machine lowers the cost of making bikes, and demand for bikes also rises. The shift in supply is larger than the shift in demand. What is the effect on the market?
opts: Quantity traded rises and price falls
Quantity traded rises and price rises
Quantity traded falls and price falls
Quantity traded falls and price rises
b.why: Both shifts are to the right, so quantity traded rises either way. The larger supply shift pulls price down more than the demand shift pushes it up, so price falls. Price would rise only if the demand shift were larger.
b.clue: Both shifts raise quantity, but they pull price in opposite ways.

a.best: Price rises and quantity traded rises

b.best: Quantity traded rises and price falls
